sn1.21:2.4: Here, as often (eg. [an6.54:22.3]()), giving up _kāmarāga_ implies attaining the absorptions. It cannot mean relinquishing the “underlying tendency” or the “fetter” to sensual desire, for this occurs only at the third stage of awakening (non-return), whereas the Buddha’s rejoinder urges rather to give up substantialist view, the first stage of awakening, the stream-enterer.
sn1.21:3.4: In some parallels for this verse, the mendicant is urged, rather, to give up desire for rebirth ([thag1.40:1.2](), [thag20.1:24.1]()). But [sn2.16:3.2]() is the same as here.
